newsitem.title: FRANCE: Guns found, 13 suspected Islamists held in France.
newsitem.headline: Guns found, 13 suspected Islamists held in France.

text.p: French police detained 13 suspected Moslem militants and found three guns at the headquarters of their group in the Paris region on Tuesday, investigators said.
The pump-action shotguns were found in a search of the headquarters of the group known as the "Muslim Association", in the western suburb of La Garenne Colombes, they said.
The swoop began after members of the group were found in a routine weekend road check to be carrying Islamic propaganda including anti-Semitic documents.
Those being held in police custody were French nationals of Algerian and Tunisian descent. Some of them were likely to be brought before a magistrate by the end of the week.
The investigators said the Muslim Association's propaganda was akin to that of the hardline Palestinian group Hamas but there did not seem to be any formal link between the two organisations.
They said the leader of the group, Maamar Metmati, was calling for violence against Jews, and one of those held had already been sentenced for assaulting a Jew.
The probe had so far failed to establish any link between the Muslim Association and Algerian rebels fighting the Algerian government and blamed for a series of bombings in France.
French police have stepped up security measures under the so-called Vigipirate plan imposed after the 1995 bombings which killed eight people.
The plan was revived after a bomb attack last December on a commuter train in Paris killed four people.
